function.description: Deploy a NEW fixed-supply ERC-20 token from the agent wallet. Takes no bytecode: it deploys one audited template whose runtime the guard asserts BYTE FOR BYTE before signing, so the token provably has no mint function, no owner, no pause and no transfer fee. The whole supply is minted to the wallet. Deploying a token does NOT make it tradable — use the launchpad for that. dry_run defaults to TRUE.
function.name: defi_trade_deploy_token

chain.description: Chain to deploy on — CHOOSE IT DELIBERATELY, because the same address is a different token on a different chain. Chains that can move value: ethereum, base, robinhood, arbitrum, polygon. Gas differs by orders of magnitude, so a cent-scale trade can cost more in gas on ethereum than it is worth, while base is a fraction of a cent. Per-chain guidance: the `chain` parameter of defi_trade.swap.

decimals.description: Decimal places. 18 is the ERC-20 norm and what every DEX assumes.

dry_run.description: TRUE (default) simulates, asserts the produced bytecode against the pinned template and reports the address it WOULD land at, without broadcasting. Set false to actually deploy.

max_spend_usd.description: The most USD this deployment may cost. A token deploy sends nothing, so this bounds the GAS FEE — on an L2 that is cents.

name.description: Token name, e.g. 'Demo Coin'. Max 64 characters, printable ASCII only.

salt.description: Leave EMPTY. A salt is REFUSED for deploy_token: through the CREATE2 factory the constructor would mint the whole supply to the factory, not the wallet, and it would be lost.

supply.description: TOTAL supply in WHOLE units, minted in full to the agent wallet. There is no mint function, so this is the supply forever. A string of digits, e.g. "1000000000" (1e9 and 1,000,000,000 also parse).

symbol.description: Ticker, e.g. 'DEMO'. Max 16 characters, printable ASCII only.

vanity.description: Leave EMPTY. A vanity prefix is REFUSED for deploy_token for the same reason as salt: the supply would be minted to the CREATE2 factory.
